providers.notes: No direct ISO boot. ARM64 import blocked by VM Import/Export. Free-tier FreeBSD AMIs available. Official AMIs for amd64 and aarch64 from FreeBSD RE.
FreeBSD 14.0+ has gVNIC preview support. Images not in default public project; must reference freebsd-org-cloud-dev. qcow2 not directly importable; must convert to raw.

Gen2 VMs use UEFI. FreeBSD in Azure Marketplace (Foundation-maintained, Q1 2025: 13.5-RELEASE). VHDX format not supported for upload despite being native to Hyper-V. Root account disabled by default in Azure FreeBSD images.
Free tier includes 4 OCPUs Ampere A1 (aarch64) - popular for FreeBSD. BYOI not supported on bare metal directly. OCI exports use .oci container format wrapping qcow2.
FreeBSD 11/12 require kernel patches not included in upstream builds. Public FreeBSD images are Alibaba-maintained with patches. Primary audience is China market.
Primary market China. International portal (intl.cloud.tencent.com) differs from domestic. FreeBSD availability in international region not fully confirmed - staleness risk.
Power Systems (ppc64le) available via IBM Power Virtual Server - separate product. Classic Infrastructure (non-VPC) has different image requirements. No native BSD support in stock catalog.
Best FreeBSD experience among mid-tier providers as of 2025. Stock images use UFS root. IPv6 available in all 33 regions. No aarch64 compute available. Max 2 custom ISOs per account.
CRITICAL: FreeBSD dropped from stock images July 2022. Must use custom image path. No aarch64 for custom images. Requires bsd-cloudinit for FreeBSD custom images. Max 100 GB uncompressed.

CRITICAL: FreeBSD not officially supported. Only ext3/ext4 accepted - rules out UFS and ZFS natively. Max 6 GB uncompressed is very small for BSD images with packages. Aarch64 available for instances but not confirmed for custom image upload.

No native image upload endpoint as of 2026-04. hcloud-upload-image is community-supported, not official. FreeBSD deployable via workaround. ARM64 (CAX) instances available. IPv6 standard on all servers.

Hetzner dropped FreeBSD rescue system - FreeBSD install now requires KVM console (paid add-on) or USB stick on request. Custom image installimage officially Linux-only. No Hetzner support for custom installs.
EFI-only for imported images is a hard constraint - BIOS-only BSD images will not boot. No FreeBSD in stock image catalog. Apple Silicon M1/M4/M4 Pro available as dedicated bare-metal Mac mini.
OpenStack under the hood gives broad compatibility. Dedicated server BYOI (separate product) supports raw/qcow2 for bare metal. Docs updated Feb 2026.
Separate product from OVHcloud Public Cloud. Full bare-metal BYOI with cloud-init for FreeBSD viable. Dedibox (dedicated) also supports FreeBSD as a stock install option.
Custom Images is a paid add-on, not included by default. amd64 only - no aarch64. qcow2 treated as pre-installed disk image. Very budget-oriented; lower SLA than Tier 1.

CRITICAL: Equinix Metal sunsets June 30, 2026. No new commercial sales. Do NOT build new genoa adapters for this target. Existing users should migrate. Alternatives: Hivelocity, phoenixNAP, Latitude.sh.
Instant-deploy server catalog. Global locations. Proxmox deployable. FreeBSD installable via iPXE or IPMI console. No aarch64 compute.
BMC = Bare Metal Cloud product. Strong API and IaC story. Custom OS details not fully public-documented without account. FreeBSD not listed as stock OS - custom path required.
Budget-oriented but reputable. KVM only for BSD. OpenVZ VPS does not support BSD. FreeBSD and other BSDs deployable with full virtualization.
Well-regarded budget BSD provider. DDoS protection included. No public API for automation. Stock BSD images may be older versions (FreeBSD 9/10/11, OpenBSD 6 per docs - check for updates).
BYOI: none. BSD: none. GPU specialist. No custom image path exists. Not suitable for genoa unless targeting ML workloads on Lambda-provided Ubuntu.
KubeVirt path makes FreeBSD theoretically deployable but not validated. Primarily GPU/ML workloads. No BSD stock images. Documentation requires account access to verify BYOI details.
Container-only BYOI, not VM image. BSD not deployable. GPU Pod model; suitable for ML workloads only from genoa perspective. Not a VM deploy target for BSD/custom OS images.
Machines product supports custom templates but only from cloning existing Linux/Windows VMs. BSD not deployable. GPU specialist. Gradient = container-only path.
Renewable/stranded energy focus differentiator. Custom image support likely but unconfirmed for BSD without account access. GPU H100/A100 focus. Small provider, growing.
OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Docker-only ingestion. Firecracker VMs are internal implementation. No path for arbitrary OS images. Global anycast edge.
OUT OF SCOPE. No VM capability at all. Isolate model (V8). No OS, no filesystem persistence, no BSD or Linux. Cloudflare Images product is CDN image optimization, not VM images.
OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Docker-only. No VM image ingestion. No custom OS.
OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Container-only.
OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. BYOC != BYOI. Container-only for workload deployment.
OUT OF SCOPE for genoa BSD/VM deploy. Interesting architecture (Firecracker + Nomad) but container-only interface. No BYOI path.
FreeBSD/OpenBSD specialist since 2008. Small but highly BSD-competent. Kernel compilation allowed. ZFS-capable. 10% discount for semi-annual/annual. US-based.
Xen hypervisor (rare among modern providers). Active FreeBSD, OpenBSD, NetBSD releases as of Dec 2025. Very small provider. NetBSD only under HVM not PV.
Duplicate of buyvm for Tier 5 BSD tracking. DDoS protection notable feature. Las Vegas NV, New York NY, Luxembourg locations.
Anthony Woodward appointed chairman March 2025 - active company. Australia-headquartered. FreeBSD on equal footing with Linux. AI infrastructure pivot with Blaize partnership.
Free and no credit card required. Not suitable for production genoa deployments. Excellent for FreeBSD/OpenBSD/NetBSD/DragonFlyBSD testing. Proxmox migration announced 2024-2025.
Unique: Raspberry Pi (aarch64) dedicated nodes as a service. Not VMs - actual Pi hardware. FreeBSD on Pi is possible but not stock. UK-based (Cambridge). From £7.14/mo.
Small specialized provider, FreeBSD and Linux/BSD dedicated servers. Not API-automated. Not suitable for genoa automated dispatch without custom integration. US West Coast only.
Apple Silicon aarch64 only. HVF hypervisor (Apple Hypervisor.framework). macOS-only VMs. Not suitable for BSD/Linux genoa deployments. macOS license requires 24h minimum.
